data.cheatsheetTitle: ac-02089 is AC-equivalent to C6; no AC path within total length 32 from ac-02089/ac-08126 to the trivial presentation or AK(3)
data.artifactTitle: ac-02089 is AC-equivalent to C6; no AC path within total length 32 from ac-02089/ac-08126 to the trivial presentation or AK(3)
data.artifactContent:
Partial result on two unresolved length-14 Miller–Schupp presentations,
$\texttt{ac-02089} = \mathrm{MS}(2,\, x^{-2}y^{-1}x^{2}y)$ and $\texttt{ac-08126} = \mathrm{MS}(2,\, x^{-2}y^{-1}x^{2}y^{-1})$.

**1. AC-equivalence (checkable certificate).** `ac-02089` is AC-equivalent to

$$C_6 = \langle x, y \mid x^2 y x^2 y^{-2},\; x y x^{-1} y^{-2} x^{-1} y \rangle,$$

one of the residual length-14 classes listed in [nahomar/andrews-curtis-solver](https://github.com/nahomar/andrews-curtis-solver). The certificate is a sequence of 1066 elementary AC moves (peak total relator length 41). Replaying it with this competition's `verifier.core.apply_move`, starting from the official initial relators of `ac-02089`, ends in the swap/inversion/rotation orbit of $C_6$. Consequently, a trivialisation of $C_6$, or an AC path from $C_6$ to `ac-00399` ($\mathrm{AK}(3)$), yields one for `ac-02089`, and conversely.

**2. Capped exhaustive search (computational, not independently verified).** For each start `ac-02089` and `ac-08126` we enumerated the complete set of presentations reachable by AC moves without the total cyclically reduced relator length exceeding $L$, for $L = 29, 30, 31, 32$. States are counted modulo relator swap, inversion, cyclic rotation and the 8 signed letter permutations; moves include conjugated multiplications with conjugators of length at most 8. The largest set has $71{,}499{,}215$ states. No set contains `ac-00399`, the trivial presentation, or the other start. Hence, in this search model, any AC path from `ac-02089` or `ac-08126` to the trivial presentation or to $\mathrm{AK}(3)$ reaches total relator length $\geq 33$. The code reproduces the cap-28 component sizes reported in nahomar/andrews-curtis-solver ($680{,}700$ and $1{,}880{,}041$).

**Open.** Whether `ac-02089`, `ac-08126` and $C_6$ are AC-trivial, or AC-equivalent to $\mathrm{AK}(3)$.

**Data.** Code, certificates, run logs and replay scripts: [alejandrozarco/andrews-curtis-ms14](https://github.com/alejandrozarco/andrews-curtis-ms14), commit `3b646c8494d0390c0df19e9e6c66aeb436f4fb7d`.

**Prior work used.**
- D. Carreras, [arXiv:2607.23611](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23611): problem context; his five certificates were used to calibrate our verifier.
- A. Shehper et al., [arXiv:2408.15332](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15332): the length-14 Miller–Schupp classification.
- [nahomar/andrews-curtis-solver](https://github.com/nahomar/andrews-curtis-solver): the residual class $C_6$; the cap-28 component sizes used for validation.
- [SAIRcompetition/Andrews-Curtis](https://github.com/SAIRcompetition/Andrews-Curtis): problem IDs; `apply_move` used for the replay.

The computations and write-up were done with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic).
